mainTopic: Which relatives by marriage may not testify, and whether a relationship that ends still disqualifies
overview: This amud works out which relatives by marriage may not testify. רב was asked whether a man may testify about his stepson's wife, and the answer is that he may not. סורא and פומבדיתא report this answer with two different reasons, and the second reason is backed by a פסוק. The גמרא then asks why the משנה lists the stepfather's son. רבי ירמיה and רב חסדא explain that line in two different ways, and they disagree about the half-brother's half-brother. Next come rulings about the fathers of a bride and groom, who may testify for each other, and about a man's betrothed wife, whom he may not testify about because he already feels close to her. The גמרא sorts out a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי about the stepson and the brother-in-law. It then brings שמואל's ruling like רבי יוסי, which leads to a real case: רב יוסף could not uphold a gift document signed by two brothers-in-law. The amud ends with rulings on whether a former relative becomes fit again, and it opens a story about מר עוקבא's in-laws that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: May a man testify about his stepson's wife?
steps.stepSummary: After the story's last word, people ask רב whether a man may testify about the wife of his stepson.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...parchment scrolls. They asked him: What is the law, may a man testify about the wife of his stepson?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story about רב and records a new question that was put to him: may a man testify about his stepson's wife? This question sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly lists close relatives who may not testify, but a stepson's wife is two steps away. She is connected to the man only through his own wife (the stepson's mother) and through her own husband (the stepson). The question is whether either of those links is enough to make her count as a relative.

keyTerms.meaning: Scrolls of parchment (the last word of the earlier story)

phrases.english: scrolls of parchment.
phrases.notes: This word finishes the story just before this, where רב went to buy parchment scrolls.

phrases.english: They asked him:
What is the law, may a man testify
about the wife of his stepson?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ: מַהוּ שֶׁיָּעִיד אָדָם בְּאֵשֶׁת חוֹרְגוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the question at the end of the earlier story
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a stepson's wife counts as a relative, so that her stepfather-in-law may not testify about her

steps.title: The סורא version: a husband is like his wife
steps.stepSummary: In סורא they report the answer as 'a husband is like his wife,' so the man may not testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they say: A husband is like his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first report of the answer, as told in סורא: a husband is treated like his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's wife is the stepson's real mother, so the stepson's wife is her daughter-in-law. If a husband is treated like his wife, then he is like a father-in-law to that woman, and he may not testify about her.

keyTerms.meaning: סורא, a major Babylonian yeshiva town
A husband is like his wife: he takes on her family relationships

phrases.english: In Sura they say:
A husband is like his wife.
phrases.notes: His wife is the stepson's mother, so he steps into her place as the young woman's in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He may not testify, because a husband takes on his wife's relationships, and she is the woman's mother-in-law

steps.title: The פומבדיתא version: a wife is like her husband
steps.stepSummary: In פומבדיתא they report the answer as 'a wife is like her husband,' which also leads to disqualifying him, but for a different reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: In פומבדיתא they say: A wife is like her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of the answer, as told in פומבדיתא: a wife is treated like her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the reasoning flips direction. The stepson himself is already disqualified, since the משנה lists one's stepson (חורגו). The stepson's wife takes on her husband's status, so she is disqualified too.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, the other major Babylonian yeshiva town
A wife is like her husband: she takes on his relationships

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions reach the same practical answer (he may not testify). They differ only in which link carries the relationship: the man through his wife, or the young woman through her husband.

phrases.english: In Pumbedita they say:
A wife is like her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the same answer
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He may not testify, because the stepson's wife takes on the status of the stepson, who is already disqualified

steps.title: A פסוק proves that a wife is like her husband
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא in the name of רב נחמן proves the rule from the פסוק that calls an uncle's wife 'your aunt.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב הונא said in the name of רב נחמן: From where do we know that a wife is like her husband? It is written: 'Do not uncover the nakedness of your father's brother; do not approach his wife, she is your aunt.' But she is only his uncle's wife! This shows that a wife is like her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the פומבדיתא idea that a wife is like her husband. The source is a פסוק about forbidden relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the uncle's wife 'your aunt,' even though she is not related by blood. She is only married to the uncle. Since the תורה gives her the uncle's family title, a wife clearly takes on her husband's relationships.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the rule: 'a husband is like his wife' (סורא) and 'a wife is like her husband' (פומבדיתא). The second has a source: the תורה calls an uncle's wife 'your aunt.'
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a wife takes on her husband's relationships becomes a basic tool for working out which in-laws may not testify.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: As Rav Huna said that Rav Naḥman said:
From where do we know that a wife is like her husband?
As it is written:
"The nakedness of your father's brother you shall not uncover;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:14

phrases.english: you shall not approach his wife;
she is your aunt."
But she is only his uncle's wife!
From this we learn that a wife is like her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מִנַּיִין שֶׁהָאִשָּׁה כְּבַעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the פומבדיתא version with a source from a פסוק
steps.raayaObject: The principle that a wife is like her husband
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 18:14, which calls the uncle's wife 'your aunt'

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the mother's husband and his family
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns back to the משנה's list: one's mother's husband, he himself, his son, and his son-in-law are disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And his mother's husband: he, his son, and his son-in-law.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה so it can examine it. This sets up the question that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a stepfather is disqualified, along with his son and his son-in-law. The גמרא is about to ask whether every item on this list is really needed.

phrases.english: And his mother's husband,
he, and his son, and his son-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה to begin a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stepfather, his son, and his son-in-law may not testify

steps.title: Isn't the stepfather's son just one's brother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה lists the stepfather's son, since that son seems to be one's brother, who is already listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: His son? That is the same as his brother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording: the son of your mother's husband looks like your own brother, and the משנה already said a brother may not testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If your mother and her husband have a son, he is your half-brother through your mother. The משנה listed 'brother' earlier, so listing 'his son' again would seem to repeat itself. The challenge assumes the משנה does not waste words.

phrases.english: His son? That is the same as his brother!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה quoted in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'his son' in the משנה's list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The stepfather's son seems to be one's half-brother, and 'brother' was already listed, so the word looks unnecessary

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: The case is the half-brother's half-brother
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains that 'the son of one's mother's husband' refers to אחי האח, a person who is not blood-related at all, and the משנה teaches that even he is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: This case is needed only for the brother of the brother.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question from Step 6. The משנה's case is not one's real brother. It is the stepfather's son from a different wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture it this way: my mother married a man and had a son, who is my maternal half-brother. That man also had a son from another wife. That son is my half-brother's half-brother but shares no parent with me. רבי ירמיה says the משנה disqualifies even him, so the line in the משנה is not repeating anything.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for... (explains the real case a line is teaching)
The brother of the brother: a half-brother's half-brother, with no shared parent

steps.confusionAlert: אחי האח is NOT your brother at all. He shares no parent with you. He is only connected to you through your half-brother.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is needed only for the brother of the brother.
phrases.notes: He means your stepfather's son from another wife. He is your half-brother's half-brother, not related to you by blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 6 by redefining the משנה's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stepfather's son is simply one's own brother, so listing him is repetitive.
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers to the stepfather's son from another wife, who is disqualified even though he is not a blood relative.

steps.title: רב חסדא allows the half-brother's half-brother to testify
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules in practice that אחי האח is a valid witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא declared the brother of the brother fit to testify.
steps.whatsHappening: We hear that רב חסדא actually ruled the opposite of רבי ירמיה. He allowed אחי האח to testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real ruling, not a theory. It directly clashes with רבי ירמיה's reading of the משנה, which sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Declared fit or valid (here, as a witness)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda declared fit the brother of the brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a ruling that disagrees with רבי ירמיה.

steps.title: The Sages ask רב חסדא if he did not hear רבי ירמיה's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The Sages challenge רב חסדא, pointing to רבי ירמיה's statement that אחי האח is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Did you not hear this teaching of רבי ירמיה?
steps.whatsHappening: The other Sages push back on רב חסדא. They assume he must not have known רבי ירמיה's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their point is that רבי ירמיה read the משנה as disqualifying אחי האח. So how could רב חסדא allow him?

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ הָא דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה?
phrases.english: Did you not hear this teaching of Rabbi Yirmeya?
phrases.notes: This is the teaching from Step 7, that the משנה disqualifies the brother of the brother.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ הָא דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's ruling from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that אחי האח may testify
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ירמיה explained the משנה as disqualifying אחי האח, so ruling him fit seems to contradict the משנה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: 'I did not hear it' means 'I do not agree'
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that he does not accept רבי ירמיה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I did not hear it. In other words, I do not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains himself. He knew the teaching, but he does not agree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'I did not hear' is a polite way of saying 'I reject this.' רב חסדא does not read the משנה the way רבי ירמיה does, so he stays with his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not hold this view

steps.confusionAlert: Do not take 'I did not hear' literally. The גמרא tells us it means he disagrees.

phrases.english: He said to them: I did not hear it,
meaning: I do not hold that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא was unaware of רבי ירמיה's teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: He knew it and rejects it.

steps.title: According to רב חסדא, the original question comes back
steps.stepSummary: If רב חסדא rejects רבי ירמיה, then 'the son of one's mother's husband' is again just one's brother, who is already in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this is the same as his brother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the question from Step 6, now according to רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה's answer is gone for רב חסדא. So the משנה's 'son of his mother's husband' seems to be his own brother again, and listing him looks repetitive.

phrases.english: If so, this is the same as his brother!
phrases.notes: 'If so' means according to רב חסדא, who rejects רבי ירמיה's answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings back the קשיא of Step 6 against רב חסדא's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of the stepfather's son, according to רב חסדא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without רבי ירמיה's reading, the stepfather's son is one's brother, who is already listed.

steps.title: The משנה lists a paternal brother and a maternal brother
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's 'his brother' means a brother from the father. 'The son of his mother's husband' means a brother from the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught his brother from the father, and it also teaches his brother from the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question for רב חסדא. The two lines are not the same person: one is a paternal brother and one is a maternal brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His brother' in the משנה refers to a brother who shares his father. 'The son of his mother's husband' is a brother who shares only his mother. So nothing repeats, and אחי האח stays a valid witness for רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: His brother from the father (paternal brother)
His brother from the mother (maternal half-brother)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה: the stepfather's son = אחי האח, and he is disqualified. רב חסדא: the stepfather's son = a maternal brother, and אחי האח may testify.

phrases.english: It taught his brother from the father,
and it also teaches his brother from the mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא אָחִיו מִן הָאָב, וְקָתָנֵי אָחִיו מִן הָאֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both lines refer to the same brother.
steps.terutzMaskana: One line is a paternal brother and the other is a maternal brother.

steps.title: Fathers of the bride and groom may testify for each other
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that אבי חתן and אבי כלה are not relatives for testimony. They are like a lid resting on a barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The father of the groom and the father of the bride may testify about each other, since they are connected to each other only like a lid on a barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling from רב חסדא. The two fathers whose children married each other may testify for one another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two fathers are linked only through their married children, not to each other directly. A lid sits on a barrel but is not part of it, and in the same way they touch without becoming relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a lid on a barrel: touching but not attached

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a limit on family disqualification: a connection made only through other people's marriage does not make two people relatives.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The father of the groom and the father of the bride
may testify about each other,
and they are not considered connected to each other
except like a lid on a barrel.
phrases.notes: A lid sits on top of the barrel but isn't part of it. The fathers touch, but they aren't family.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֲבִי חָתָן וַאֲבִי כַּלָּה מְעִידִין זֶה עַל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about relatives through marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבי חתן and אבי כלה may testify for each other, because they are not relatives.

steps.title: A man may testify for his betrothed wife
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה rules that a man may testify for his אשתו ארוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: A man may testify for his betrothed wife.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the list of who counts as a relative for testimony, the גמרא brings a new ruling: a man may testify about his אשתו ארוסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who has had אירוסין is legally his wife, but they do not live together yet. רבה בר בר חנה holds that at this stage she is not yet treated as his relative, so his testimony about her is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: his betrothed wife, after אירוסין but before נישואין

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
A man may testify for his betrothed wife.
phrases.notes: Betrothed here means after the first stage of marriage, before the wedding. She is already his wife in a legal sense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like step 13, this defines one more pair that does or does not count as relatives for testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man is a valid witness regarding his אשתו ארוסה.

steps.title: Only when the testimony takes money away from her
steps.stepSummary: רבינא limits the ruling: it applies only to testimony that removes money from her, not testimony that gives her money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: We said this only when his testimony takes money away from her. But when it brings money to her, he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא narrows רבה בר בר חנה's ruling so it only covers testimony that works against her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony against her is believable, because he has no reason to lie and hurt her. Testimony that helps her is suspect, because he will soon marry her and gain from her money.

keyTerms.meaning: to take money out of her hands
to bring money in to her

phrases.english: Ravina said:
We said this only for taking money out from her,
but for bringing money in to her, he is not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 14 to testimony that goes against her.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His testimony is accepted only when it goes against her financial interest.

steps.title: He is not believed either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the ruling: whether the testimony helps her or hurts her, he is not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. It makes no difference whether it takes money away or brings money in: he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects what was said in steps 14-15 and rules that a man can never testify about his אשתו ארוסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ולא היא' signal that the גמרא does not accept the earlier position. Even testimony against her is invalid. This means the disqualification is not about suspected lying. She simply counts as close to him already.

keyTerms.meaning: but it is not so (the גמרא rejecting a view)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he is disqualified only because he might lie to help her. He is disqualified even when his testimony hurts her, so the issue is closeness, not money.

phrases.english: But it is not so;
there is no difference whether it is to take money out
and no difference whether it is to bring money in; he is not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects both רבה בר בר חנה's ruling and רבינא's limit on it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the entire idea that a man may testify about his אשתו ארוסה, both in רבה בר בר חנה's form and in רבינא's limited form.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Treating the betrothed woman as not close to him. In fact she is close enough to disqualify him in every case.

steps.title: What was the lenient view based on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reasoning led to the view that he may testify about his betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is your thinking?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking why anyone thought a betrothed woman does not count as a relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having rejected the lenient view, the גמרא wants to uncover its source. That way it can show where the reasoning went wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: what is your thinking? what were you basing this on?

phrases.english: What is your thinking?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking the one who said he may testify (step 14) what he was relying on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the lenient view, the גמרא asks for its basis.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or logic behind treating an אשתו ארוסה as a non-relative for testimony.

steps.title: The source: עולא's rule that a betrothed wife is not like a relative
steps.stepSummary: The lenient view relied on עולא: a man and his betrothed do not mourn for each other, do not become טמא for each other, and he does not inherit her.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא: For his betrothed wife, a man does not become an אונן and does not become impure for her. Likewise, she does not become an אוננת for him and does not become impure for him. If she dies, he does not inherit her. If he dies, she collects her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The lenient view was based on עולא's rule that, in many areas of הלכה, a betrothed woman is not treated as a close relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is the logic. In אנינות, טומאה for a כהן, and ירושה, she is not treated as his relative. So it seemed she should not count as a relative for testimony either. Her collecting the כתובה is just a debt he owes her, not a sign of family closeness.

keyTerms.meaning: a mourner on the day of a close relative's death, before burial
becomes ritually impure (a כהן may do so only for close relatives)

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla:
For his betrothed wife, he does not become an onen,
and he does not become impure for her,
phrases.notes: This is talking about a כהן, who may only become impure through a dead body for his close relatives.

phrases.english: and likewise, she does not become an onenet,
and does not become impure for him.
If she died, he does not inherit her;
if he died, she collects her כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by naming the source of the lenient view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lenient view was based on עולא: in mourning, טומאה and inheritance, a betrothed woman is not treated as his relative.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא בר אמי in the name of עולא

steps.title: Testimony is about closeness, not legal kinship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. טומאה depends on 'his kin', which she is not yet. Testimony depends on emotional closeness, which he already feels.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the תורה made the law depend on 'his kin,' and she is not yet his kin. Here, the reason is closeness of mind, and his mind is already close to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why עולא's rule does not prove anything about testimony. That is why the final ruling of step 16 stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of טומאה and mourning depend on a legal status, 'שארו', which only comes with נישואין. The disqualification from testimony comes from personal attachment, אקרובי דעתא. A man feels that attachment to the woman he is engaged to marry. Different reasons, so different results.

keyTerms.meaning: his kin, his close relative (here, his wife after נישואין)
the Torah made it depend on

steps.whatToRemember: A man cannot testify for or against his אשתו ארוסה. Even though she is not yet 'שארו' for טומאה and inheritance, he already feels close to her, and that closeness is what disqualifies a witness.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that disqualifying relatives from testimony can rest on emotional closeness, not only on formal family status. That is why a betrothed woman counts here but not for טומאה.

phrases.english: There, the Merciful One made it depend on "his kin,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:2

phrases.english: and she is not yet his kin.
Here, it is because of closeness of mind,
and his mind has indeed become close to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 18, which supports the ruling of step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using עולא's rule as proof about testimony.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two areas rest on different reasons. טומאה depends on the legal status 'שארו', while testimony depends on emotional closeness, which already exists at אירוסין.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A man is not believed in testimony about his אשתו ארוסה in any case, because he already feels close to her.

steps.title: Two teachings argue about the stepson and the brother-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'his stepson alone' and brings two ברייתות. In them רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about whether it is the stepson or the brother-in-law who is disqualified 'alone'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'His stepson alone.' A ברייתא teaches: His stepson alone is disqualified. רבי יוסי says: His brother-in-law. Another ברייתא teaches: His brother-in-law alone. רבי יהודה says: His stepson.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה's phrase 'his stepson alone' and brings two ברייתות that show a מחלוקת about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Alone' means only the relative himself is disqualified, not his son or son-in-law. The two ברייתות together show that the anonymous view in the first one is רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה says the stepson is 'alone', and רבי יוסי says the brother-in-law is 'alone'.

keyTerms.meaning: His stepson (his wife's son from another man)
Alone: only the relative himself, not his son or son-in-law

phrases.english: His stepson alone.
phrases.notes: These words are quoted from our משנה, which lists the relatives who may not testify.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: His stepson alone.
Rabbi Yosei says: His brother-in-law.
And another [ברייתא] teaches: His brother-in-law alone.
Rabbi Yehuda says: His stepson.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, moving from a man and his betrothed to the משנה's phrase about the stepson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה says the stepson is disqualified alone; רבי יוסי says the brother-in-law is disqualified alone.

steps.title: First reading: both relatives are disqualified alone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means. It suggests that both תנאים agree that both the stepson and the brother-in-law are disqualified alone, and they only differ in which one they mention.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying? If you say it means this: His stepson alone, and the same is true for his brother-in-law. And רבי יוסי comes to say: His brother-in-law alone, and the same is true for his stepson.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the argument is really about. It offers a first reading and is setting up a challenge to it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading there is no real disagreement in the law. Both relatives are disqualified only by themselves. Each תנא just mentions a different example.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be challenged)
And the same law applies to

phrases.english: What is it saying?
If you say it is saying this:
His stepson alone, and the same is true for his brother-in-law.
And Rabbi Yosei comes to say:
His brother-in-law alone, and the same is true for his stepson.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the מחלוקת in the ברייתות means and offers a first reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly do רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי disagree about?

steps.title: Then whose view is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה disqualifies the brother-in-law together with his son and son-in-law. In the first reading, neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי holds that.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then the משנה, which teaches 'his brother-in-law, he and his son and his son-in-law', whose view is it? Neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first reading. It would leave our משנה with no תנא to match it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה clearly says the brother-in-law's son and son-in-law are disqualified too. If both תנאים limit the brother-in-law to himself alone, then nobody holds like the משנה. So the first reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: He, his son and his son-in-law

phrases.english: But our משנה, which teaches:
His brother-in-law, he and his son and his son-in-law,

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּי? לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: Whose is it? Neither Rabbi Yehuda nor Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first reading offered in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that both תנאים limit both relatives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה disqualifies the brother-in-law's son and son-in-law, so in that reading it fits neither תנא.

steps.title: Second reading: each limits only one relative
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the מחלוקת differently. רבי יהודה limits the stepson but includes the brother-in-law's son and son-in-law. רבי יוסי does the reverse. Now the משנה fits רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means this: His stepson alone, but his brother-in-law, he and his son and his son-in-law. And רבי יוסי comes to say: His brother-in-law alone, but his stepson, he and his son and his son-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new reading of the ברייתות that solves the problem with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is a real argument about the law. Each תנא says that one relative is disqualified alone and the other is disqualified with his son and son-in-law. Our משנה matches רבי יהודה exactly: the stepson is alone, and the brother-in-law comes with his son and son-in-law.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it is saying
But (shows the contrast between the two relatives)

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, our משנה follows רבי יהודה: the stepson alone, but the brother-in-law with his son and son-in-law.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:
His stepson alone,
but his brother-in-law: he and his son and his son-in-law.
And Rabbi Yosei comes to say:
His brother-in-law alone,
but his stepson: he and his son and his son-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 22 by reading the ברייתות a new way.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both תנאים limit both relatives to themselves alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each תנא limits only one relative and includes the other's son and son-in-law; the משנה follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Then whose view is רבי חייא's 'twenty-four'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא taught that eight main relatives, each with his son and son-in-law, make twenty-four. That count leaves out the son and son-in-law of both the stepson and the brother-in-law. In the second reading, each תנא adds one of them as a ninth relative, so neither fits.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what רבי חייא taught, 'eight fathers, which are twenty-four', whose view is it? It is neither like רבי יוסי nor like רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty against the second reading. Now a ברייתא of רבי חייא has no תנא to match it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eight times three (the man, his son and his son-in-law) equals twenty-four. So only eight relatives bring along their sons and sons-in-law, and the stepson and brother-in-law are not among them. In the second reading, רבי יהודה adds the brother-in-law's son and son-in-law, and רבי יוסי adds the stepson's, which makes nine 'fathers' and twenty-seven people, so רבי חייא agrees with neither.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose view is this?

phrases.english: But then, this that Rabbi Chiya taught:
Eight fathers, which are twenty-four,
phrases.notes: Each of the eight main relatives counts three times: himself, his son and his son-in-law. That makes 24.

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַאן? לָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה!
phrases.english: Like whom? Neither like Rabbi Yosei nor like Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second reading from step 23 using רבי חייא's ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that each תנא limits one relative to himself alone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא counts only eight relatives with their sons and sons-in-law, which leaves out the families of both the stepson and the brother-in-law. In this reading each תנא includes one of those families, so the count would be more than twenty-four.

steps.title: A new reading: the משנה follows רבי יהודה and the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא a new way. רבי יהודה: the stepson alone is disqualified, but the brother-in-law is disqualified together with his son and son-in-law. רבי יוסי: the brother-in-law alone, and all the more so the stepson. So the משנה follows רבי יהודה and רבי חייא's ברייתא follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it means: his stepson alone is disqualified, but his brother-in-law is disqualified together with his son and his son-in-law. And רבי יוסי comes to say: his brother-in-law alone, and all the more so his stepson. So the משנה follows רבי יהודה, and the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from רבי חייא's list by reading the מחלוקת a new way. It then tells us which תנא each source follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' changes only how רבי יוסי is read. רבי יהודה stays the same (stepson alone, brother-in-law with his son and son-in-law), which fits the משנה. Now רבי יוסי holds that both the brother-in-law and the stepson are disqualified alone, so only the other eight relatives come with sons and sons-in-law, which gives exactly רבי חייא's twenty-four.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what he means (the earlier reading is dropped)
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: In the end: the משנה follows רבי יהודה, and רבי חייא's ברייתא follows רבי יוסי.
steps.confusionAlert: There are now two different 'רבי יוסי' positions. One is in the משנה, where he lets a brother-in-law testify. The other is in the ברייתא, where 'his brother-in-law alone' is disqualified. Keep them apart, because the next steps depend on it.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:
His stepson alone is disqualified,
but his brother-in-law is disqualified, he, his son, and his son-in-law.
And רבי יוסי comes to say:
His brother-in-law alone, and all the more so his stepson.
And our משנה follows רבי יהודה,
and the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי.
phrases.notes: This is רבי חייא's ברייתא of twenty-four relatives from the step before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from רבי חייא's ברייתא by reading the מחלוקת a new way
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the ברייתא, so that each source is matched to one תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier reading left רבי חייא's ברייתא without any תנא it fits
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, and the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה is like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives the practical ruling: we follow רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is short and does not say which רבי יוסי it means, the one in the משנה or the one in the ברייתא. That gap is exactly what the next two steps argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: רב יהודה quoting his teacher שמואל

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the basis for the real case that comes next.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that שמואל said:
The הלכה is like רבי יוסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling after the opinions were sorted out

steps.title: רב יוסף wants to accept a gift document signed by two brothers-in-law
steps.stepSummary: A gift document was signed by two witnesses who were brothers-in-law. רב יוסף thought to accept it, because שמואל ruled like רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain gift document signed by two brothers-in-law. רב יוסף thought to accept it, because רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה is like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case where רב יוסף uses שמואל's ruling to accept witnesses who are brothers-in-law. This sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף understood שמואל to mean the רבי יוסי of the משנה, who lets a brother-in-law testify. So for him, two brothers-in-law can be valid witnesses together. The next step questions that assumption.

phrases.english: There was a certain gift document
on which two brothers-in-law were signed as witnesses.
רב יוסף thought to accept it as valid,
because רב יהודה said that שמואל said:
The הלכה is like רבי יוסי.
phrases.notes: רב יוסף took this to mean the רבי יוסי of the משנה, as אביי's question in the next step shows.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא מַתַּנְתָּא דַּהֲווֹ חֲתִימִי עֲלַהּ תְּרֵי גִּיסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses שמואל's ruling in a real case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף wants to accept the document, based on שמואל's ruling like רבי יוסי

steps.title: אביי: maybe שמואל meant the רבי יוסי of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף how he knows that שמואל meant the רבי יוסי of the משנה, who lets a brother-in-law testify. Maybe he meant the רבי יוסי of the ברייתא, who disqualifies the brother-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: How do you know שמואל meant the רבי יוסי of the משנה, who lets a brother-in-law testify? Maybe he meant the רבי יוסי of the ברייתא, who disqualifies a brother-in-law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's decision to accept the document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two 'רבי יוסי' positions about a brother-in-law, and they point in opposite directions. שמואל's ruling did not say which one he meant. If he meant the ברייתא, the two brothers-in-law are not valid witnesses and the document should not be accepted.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not arguing with שמואל's ruling. He is only asking which רבי יוסי שמואל meant.

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
From where do you know that שמואל meant the רבי יוסי of our משנה,
who lets a brother-in-law testify?
Perhaps he meant the רבי יוסי of the ברייתא,
who disqualifies a brother-in-law?
phrases.notes: This is 'his brother-in-law alone' from step 25: the brother-in-law himself is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מִמַּאי דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how רב יוסף applied שמואל's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's decision to accept a document signed by two brothers-in-law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's ruling could mean the רבי יוסי of the ברייתא, who disqualifies a brother-in-law, so the document might not be valid

steps.title: רב יוסף proves שמואל meant the lenient רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers אביי from another statement of שמואל: he and פנחס cannot testify for each other because they are both brothers and brothers-in-law. This implies that ordinary brothers-in-law may testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that. שמואל said: 'For example, פנחס and I, who are brothers and also brothers-in-law.' This implies that ordinary brothers-in-law are fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his ruling. He shows that שמואל himself said ordinary brothers-in-law may testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל and his brother פנחס married two sisters, so they are related in two ways. שמואל gave himself and פנחס as his example of who is disqualified, and he mentioned both connections. רב יוסף reads this to mean that a brother-in-law connection alone does not disqualify, which fits the רבי יוסי of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't let that enter your mind. It rejects a suggestion.
Ordinary brothers-in-law, who are not also brothers
It is fine, it is permitted

phrases.english: Don't let it enter your mind,
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף answering אביי. He rejects the idea that שמואל meant the strict רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: for שמואל said:
For example, Pinchas and I,
phrases.notes: פנחס was שמואל's brother.

phrases.english: who are brothers and brothers-in-law,
but ordinary brothers-in-law are fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from step 28 about which רבי יוסי שמואל meant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from another statement by the same אמורא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל might have meant the רבי יוסי of the ברייתא, who disqualifies a brother-in-law.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל said he and פנחס are disqualified because they are both brothers and brothers-in-law, so a plain brother-in-law is a valid witness.

steps.title: Maybe שמואל mentioned the brother-in-law link as the real reason
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. Perhaps שמואל said 'Pinchas and I' because of the brother-in-law connection, and that alone is what disqualifies them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps when he said 'for example, פנחס and I,' he said it because פנחס was his brother-in-law?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's proof. He reads שמואל's words the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed that both connections had to be present for the disqualification. The other reading is that שמואל mentioned the brother-in-law connection to show that it alone disqualifies. If so, שמואל agrees with the strict רבי יוסי of the ברייתא, and the gift document is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps. It offers another possible reading.

steps.confusionAlert: Being a brother would disqualify them anyway. The question is only why שמואל also mentioned the brother-in-law connection: was it to say that both were needed, or to say that this alone disqualifies?

phrases.english: But perhaps,
when he said 'for example, Pinchas and I,'
he said it because פנחס was his brother-in-law?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא, כְּגוֹן אֲנָא וּפִנְחָס, מִשּׁוּם גִיסוֹ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 29.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from שמואל's example of himself and פנחס
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The example can be read to mean that the brother-in-law connection alone disqualifies. So it does not prove that ordinary brothers-in-law are valid.

steps.title: רב יוסף tries to save the gift through the handover witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף accepts the objection. He tells the holder of the document to acquire the gift through the witnesses who saw the document handed over, following רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go, acquire it through the witnesses who saw the handing over, following רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the signing witnesses may be invalid, רב יוסף looks for another way to make the gift work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, the witnesses who see a document being handed over are the ones who make the deal take effect. The signatures only add strength to the document. So even if the signers are invalid, the gift should stand if valid witnesses saw the handover.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who see the document being handed over
The תנא who holds that the handover witnesses make a document take effect

phrases.english: He said to him: Go,
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is now talking to the person holding the gift document.

phrases.english: acquire it through the witnesses who saw it handed over,
following רבי אלעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל, קַנְיַהּ בְּעֵדֵי מְסִירָה, כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 29 was rejected, רב יוסף switches to another way of saving the gift.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gift can be acquired through valid handover witnesses, following רבי אלעזר, even if the signing witnesses are questionable.

steps.title: Even רבי אלעזר rejects a document with invalid signatures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this using רבי אבא: רבי אלעזר agrees that a document which is faulty from within, such as one signed by invalid witnesses, is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אבא say that רבי אלעזר agrees that a document forged from within is invalid?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's new solution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Signatures may not be needed according to רבי אלעזר. Still, if the document itself carries invalid signatures, the flaw sits inside the document, and רבי אלעזר admits such a document is invalid. This document is signed by two brothers-in-law who may be invalid witnesses, so the handover witnesses cannot save it.

keyTerms.meaning: Forged from within: the flaw is in the document itself, such as invalid signatures

phrases.english: But didn't רבי אבא say:
רבי אלעזר agrees
that a document forged from within is invalid?
phrases.notes: Here that means a document signed by witnesses who are not allowed to sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בִּמְזוּיָּף מִתּוֹכוֹ שֶׁהוּא פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's solution from step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling to acquire the gift through the handover witnesses, following רבי אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר himself agrees that a document with invalid signatures is invalid, so the handover witnesses cannot rescue this document.

steps.title: רב יוסף cannot validate the gift
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives up and tells the holder that the rabbis will not let him uphold the document for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go. They won't let me settle it for you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף concludes that he cannot uphold the gift document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ways of saving the document have fallen. It is unclear whether שמואל allows brothers-in-law to sign, and the handover witnesses do not help when the signatures are invalid. So רב יוסף sends the holder away without a ruling in his favor.

keyTerms.meaning: To settle it for you, to uphold it in your favor

steps.whatToRemember: A document signed by two brothers-in-law is not upheld. It is not clear that שמואל ruled like the lenient רבי יוסי, and even רבי אלעזר rejects a document whose own signatures are invalid.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that invalid signers ruin a document even according to the view that signatures are not what makes it take effect.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go,
they won't let me settle it for you.
phrases.notes: Literally 'to seat it for you.' He means the rabbis won't let him uphold the gift in your favor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל, לָא שָׁבְקִי לִי דְּאוֹתְבִינֵּיהּ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge in step 32 and ends the case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The gift document signed by two brothers-in-law is not upheld.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's view from the משנה, and רב, through a chain of rabbis, rules like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says, etc. רבי תנחום said in the name of רבי טבלא, in the name of רבי ברונא, in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes רבי יהודה's opinion from the משנה and brings רב's ruling that the הלכה follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה says that a son-in-law whose wife died stays disqualified if he has children from her, because the family link continues through the children. רב rules that this is the הלכה. The ruling is passed down through three rabbis before it reaches us.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion
Etc.: the quote from the משנה continues
The תנא who holds that the relationship stays alive through children

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: if he has children from the litigant's daughter, he stays disqualified even after she dies.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי טַבְלָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum said that Rabbi Tavla said
that Rabbi Beruna said that Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the story of רב יוסף and the document ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, a former son-in-law with children from the litigant's daughter stays disqualified.

steps.title: רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן rule against רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא, quoting רב נחמן, says the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה. רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן saying the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: The הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה. And likewise רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more authorities rule the opposite of רב: the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן, once the wife who created the relationship has died, the man is no longer a relative, even if he has children from her. This sides with the תנא קמא of the משנה. The word וכן shows that רבי יוחנן agrees with רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: The law does not follow this opinion
And likewise: another authority says the same thing

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Nachman said:
The halacha does not follow Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: And likewise Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha does not follow Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite ruling to רב's ruling in step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the connecting wife has died, the former son-in-law is fit, even if he has children from her.

steps.title: Another version: רבי יוסי הגלילי's דרשה about a former relative
steps.stepSummary: Some teach רבה בר בר חנה's ruling as a comment on a different source: רבי יוסי הגלילי's דרשה on the פסוק "the judge who will be in those days."
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this statement of רבה בר בר חנה as a comment on this: רבי יוסי הגלילי expounded this פסוק: "And you shall come to the כהנים, the לוים, and to the judge who will be in those days." Could you imagine that a person goes to a judge who was not in his days? Rather, it refers to one who was a relative and became distant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of where רבה בר בר חנה's ruling was said. First it sets up the source that the ruling refers to, רבי יוסי הגלילי's דרשה. The ruling itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי notes that the words "in those days" seem unnecessary, since nobody goes to a judge who lives in another time. So he explains them as teaching about a judge who was once related to a litigant and no longer is: in "those days" he is fit. In this version, רבי יוחנן's ruling is not phrased as a rejection of רבי יהודה. It is phrased as agreement with רבי יוסי הגלילי.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it this way: a different version of where a statement belongs
Expounded: learned a lesson from a פסוק
Could it enter your mind?: the words seem obvious, so they must teach something new
Was a relative and became distant: the family connection ended

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same ruling of רבי יוחנן, which some teach in connection with a different source.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it

phrases.aramaic: לְהָא דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אַהָא:
phrases.english: this statement of Rabba bar bar Chana as referring to this:

phrases.aramaic: אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili expounded this verse:
"And you shall come to the Kohanim, the Levites,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶל הַשֹּׁפֵט אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם״.
phrases.english: and to the judge who will be in those days."
phrases.notes: דברים 17:9

phrases.english: Could it enter your mind
that a person goes to a judge
who did not live in his days?
Rather, this is one who was a relative and became distant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אַהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of where רבה בר בר חנה's statement from step 35 was said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, a former relative whose connection ended may serve as a judge.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי: a former relative is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: This completes the second version. רבי יוחנן's ruling is stated as agreement with רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practical result is the same as in step 35. Once the relationship has ended, the person may testify or judge. The only difference between the two versions is which source the ruling was attached to.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who expounded "in those days" as referring to a former relative
An אמורא who passes on רבי יוחנן's rulings

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions lead to the same practical ruling from רבי יוחנן: someone who was related by marriage and is no longer related is fit as a witness and as a judge.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling that the second version attaches to רבי יוסי הגלילי's דרשה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי: a former relative is fit.

steps.title: A story begins: the sons of מר עוקבא's father-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story about the sons of מר עוקבא's father-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons of the father-in-law of מר עוקבא...
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up a story that continues in the next part of the גמרא. It only introduces the people in the story, so wait for the rest before drawing conclusions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people introduced are relatives of מר עוקבא through his marriage. That fits the topic of relatives by marriage. What happened with them comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who served as a judge

phrases.english: The sons of the father-in-law of Mar Ukva

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rulings to a story about relatives by marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the people in a story about מר עוקבא's in-laws; no ruling has been given yet.
